newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ICI says can't explain share rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ICI says can't explain share rise.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd said on Thursday it could not explain the recent rise in its share price.

The company also said in response to a query from the Australian Stock Exchange that it had also informed the market that its profit in the year to September 30 was likely to be below the 1994/95 result.

"We are not aware of any information which if publicly available would provide an explanation for the recent share price increases," ICI Australia managing director Warren Haynes said. "We have informed the market that our profit expectations for the year ending September 30th are likely to be below previous year. This can be at a rate of more than 15 percent."
The exchange queried the ICI share move after the company's shares ended 28 cents up at A$12.88, a record high. This compares with a share price of A$11.15 on September 25.

Haynes said there will be abnormal charges which have already been announced to the market. On April 30, ICI Australia said it expected to report an abnormal charge of A$10-15 million in the second half of the financial year to September 30, 1996.

There were market rumours on Thursday that ICI Australia's parent Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc would launch a bid to mop up the 37.5 percent it does not already own in its Austrlian offshoot, brokers said.
Based on Thursday's closing price the 37.5 percent stake is valued at A$1.4 billion.

"The same speculation (of an ICI Plc takeover) pops up every four or five months. Today I think it has been helped by yesterday's bid for TNT -- its (ICI Australia's) turnover has been higher than usual today," a Melbourne-based broker said.
About 430,000 ICI Australia shares were traded on Thursday.
"We cannot comment on any rumours in the marketplace," said a spokeswoman for ICI Australia.
"Our managing director won't be commenting on these rumours either. They have been around for the past three years and that has always been our stance," she said.
